properties.name: Shelby County Historical Society Museum
properties.title: Shelby County Historical Society Museum
properties.history: Local history museum in an 1872 downtown Shelbyville building operated by the Shelby County Historical Society. Exhibits cover county settlement, farming, and community life near the Frankfort-to-Falls road that made Shelbyville a county seat. Free admission for drop-in visitors exploring Bluegrass county heritage.
properties.description: Local history museum in an 1872 downtown Shelbyville building operated by the Shelby County Historical Society. Exhibits cover county settlement, farming, and community life near the Frankfort-to-Falls road that made Shelbyville a county seat. Free admission for drop-in visitors exploring Bluegrass county heritage.

properties.name: Anderson County History Museum
properties.title: Anderson County History Museum
properties.history: Housed in Lawrenceburg's 1908 Carnegie Library, this free museum displays artifacts that tell Anderson County's story from pioneer settlement through bourbon-country commerce. Regular Tuesday open hours plus appointment visits make it a practical stop near Wild Turkey and Four Roses country.
properties.description: Housed in Lawrenceburg's 1908 Carnegie Library, this free museum displays artifacts that tell Anderson County's story from pioneer settlement through bourbon-country commerce. Regular Tuesday open hours plus appointment visits make it a practical stop near Wild Turkey and Four Roses country.

properties.name: Thomas D. Clark Center for Kentucky History
properties.title: Thomas D. Clark Center for Kentucky History
properties.history: Flagship museum of the Kentucky Historical Society covering more than 12,000 years of Kentucky history, with permanent and rotating exhibits plus a major research library. Anchors the Frankfort history campus a short walk from the Old Capitol and Military History Museum. Smithsonian Affiliate and a natural first stop for statewide context.
properties.description: Flagship museum of the Kentucky Historical Society covering more than 12,000 years of Kentucky history, with permanent and rotating exhibits plus a major research library. Anchors the Frankfort history campus a short walk from the Old Capitol and Military History Museum. Smithsonian Affiliate and a natural first stop for statewide context.

properties.name: Old State Capitol
properties.title: Old State Capitol
properties.history: Gideon Shryock's Greek Revival capitol (completed 1830) served as Kentucky's seat of government until 1910 and is now interpreted by the Kentucky Historical Society. The building and public grounds tell the story of antebellum politics, Civil War-era Frankfort, and statehouse architecture. Pair with the Clark Center across Broadway.
properties.description: Gideon Shryock's Greek Revival capitol (completed 1830) served as Kentucky's seat of government until 1910 and is now interpreted by the Kentucky Historical Society. The building and public grounds tell the story of antebellum politics, Civil War-era Frankfort, and statehouse architecture. Pair with the Clark Center across Broadway.

properties.name: Kentucky Military History Museum
properties.title: Kentucky Military History Museum
properties.history: Located in the fortress-like 1850 State Arsenal overlooking downtown Frankfort, this KHS museum interprets Kentucky military service through personal stories and artifacts. The Arsenal supplied arms through the Civil War and National Guard eras before becoming a museum in 1974. Part of the Army Museum System.
properties.description: Located in the fortress-like 1850 State Arsenal overlooking downtown Frankfort, this KHS museum interprets Kentucky military service through personal stories and artifacts. The Arsenal supplied arms through the Civil War and National Guard eras before becoming a museum in 1974. Part of the Army Museum System.

properties.name: Capital City Museum
properties.title: Capital City Museum
properties.history: Downtown Frankfort museum focused on the everyday life of the capital city—politics, industry, neighborhoods, and river commerce. Complements the statewide story at the Clark Center with a tighter local lens. Easy walking distance from Liberty Hall and the history campus.
properties.description: Downtown Frankfort museum focused on the everyday life of the capital city—politics, industry, neighborhoods, and river commerce. Complements the statewide story at the Clark Center with a tighter local lens. Easy walking distance from Liberty Hall and the history campus.

properties.name: Liberty Hall Historic Site
properties.title: Liberty Hall Historic Site
properties.history: Two historic houses on the Kentucky River: Liberty Hall (1796) and the Orlando Brown House (1835), set in gardens in downtown Frankfort. Interprets early Kentucky political and family life tied to the Brown family and the young capital. Guided tours and grounds visits from spring through fall.
properties.description: Two historic houses on the Kentucky River: Liberty Hall (1796) and the Orlando Brown House (1835), set in gardens in downtown Frankfort. Interprets early Kentucky political and family life tied to the Brown family and the young capital. Guided tours and grounds visits from spring through fall.

properties.name: Oldham County History Center
properties.title: Oldham County History Center
properties.history: Campus of the Oldham County Historical Society west of the courthouse square, including the Peyton Samuel Head Family Museum, archives, and Rob Morris Chapel. Strong Underground Railroad interpretation (NPS Passport site) plus exhibits on D.W. Griffith, WWII veterans, and the Kentucky State Reformatory. Hands-on discovery museum for all ages.
properties.description: Campus of the Oldham County Historical Society west of the courthouse square, including the Peyton Samuel Head Family Museum, archives, and Rob Morris Chapel. Strong Underground Railroad interpretation (NPS Passport site) plus exhibits on D.W. Griffith, WWII veterans, and the Kentucky State Reformatory. Hands-on discovery museum for all ages.

properties.name: Woodford County Historical Society Museum
properties.title: Woodford County Historical Society Museum
properties.history: Free museum of Woodford County artifacts including Civil War memorabilia, everyday textiles and tools, and photographs of 1890s county schools. Displays also highlight Woodford's six Kentucky governors and Versailles streetscape history. Compact downtown stop near horse-farm country.
properties.description: Free museum of Woodford County artifacts including Civil War memorabilia, everyday textiles and tools, and photographs of 1890s county schools. Displays also highlight Woodford's six Kentucky governors and Versailles streetscape history. Compact downtown stop near horse-farm country.

properties.name: Bluegrass Railroad and Museum
properties.title: Bluegrass Railroad and Museum
properties.history: Heritage railroad and museum in Woodford County Park offering scenic excursions through Bluegrass farmland plus rolling-stock and railroad history exhibits. A family-friendly outdoor stop that pairs well with Versailles and Midway bourbon-and-horse country drives.
properties.description: Heritage railroad and museum in Woodford County Park offering scenic excursions through Bluegrass farmland plus rolling-stock and railroad history exhibits. A family-friendly outdoor stop that pairs well with Versailles and Midway bourbon-and-horse country drives.

properties.name: Jack Jouett House Historic Site
properties.title: Jack Jouett House Historic Site
properties.history: Late-18th-century home of Revolutionary War hero Jack Jouett—the 'Paul Revere of the South' who rode to warn Jefferson and the Virginia legislature in 1781. Interprets frontier architecture and Jouett's later Kentucky years. Rural Woodford County setting southwest of Versailles.
properties.description: Late-18th-century home of Revolutionary War hero Jack Jouett—the 'Paul Revere of the South' who rode to warn Jefferson and the Virginia legislature in 1781. Interprets frontier architecture and Jouett's later Kentucky years. Rural Woodford County setting southwest of Versailles.

properties.name: Georgetown & Scott County Museum
properties.title: Georgetown & Scott County Museum
properties.history: Public museum in the former Georgetown Post Office collecting and interpreting Scott County history, culture, and artifacts. Exhibits and a gift shop of local art sit on Main Street in a growing Toyota-era college town. Strong local-history stop between Lexington and Cincinnati.
properties.description: Public museum in the former Georgetown Post Office collecting and interpreting Scott County history, culture, and artifacts. Exhibits and a gift shop of local art sit on Main Street in a growing Toyota-era college town. Strong local-history stop between Lexington and Cincinnati.

properties.name: Ward Hall
properties.title: Ward Hall
properties.history: Monumental Greek Revival mansion built in the 1850s for Junius Ward—one of Kentucky's grandest antebellum houses. Tours interpret plantation-era architecture, Scott County society, and the building's later preservation. Landmark drive-to stop on the edge of Georgetown.
properties.description: Monumental Greek Revival mansion built in the 1850s for Junius Ward—one of Kentucky's grandest antebellum houses. Tours interpret plantation-era architecture, Scott County society, and the building's later preservation. Landmark drive-to stop on the edge of Georgetown.

properties.name: Frazier History Museum
properties.title: Frazier History Museum
properties.history: Museum Row flagship telling Kentucky history, culture, and people—including the official Kentucky Bourbon Trail Welcome Center. Combines arms-and-armor roots with rotating exhibits on Commonwealth stories. Ideal downtown starting point for Louisville history days.
properties.description: Museum Row flagship telling Kentucky history, culture, and people—including the official Kentucky Bourbon Trail Welcome Center. Combines arms-and-armor roots with rotating exhibits on Commonwealth stories. Ideal downtown starting point for Louisville history days.

properties.name: Kentucky Derby Museum
properties.title: Kentucky Derby Museum
properties.history: Thoroughbred racing museum at Churchill Downs covering Derby history, jockeys, trainers, and race-day culture. Immersive exhibits and track tours connect Louisville's most famous tradition to the wider horse industry. Essential sports-and-culture stop in Jefferson County.
properties.description: Thoroughbred racing museum at Churchill Downs covering Derby history, jockeys, trainers, and race-day culture. Immersive exhibits and track tours connect Louisville's most famous tradition to the wider horse industry. Essential sports-and-culture stop in Jefferson County.

properties.name: Louisville Slugger Museum & Factory
properties.title: Louisville Slugger Museum & Factory
properties.history: Museum and working bat factory on Main Street celebrating baseball and the iconic Louisville Slugger brand. Factory tours, player exhibits, and the giant bat outside make it one of Louisville's most recognizable visitor stops. Anchors Museum Row beside the Frazier.
properties.description: Museum and working bat factory on Main Street celebrating baseball and the iconic Louisville Slugger brand. Factory tours, player exhibits, and the giant bat outside make it one of Louisville's most recognizable visitor stops. Anchors Museum Row beside the Frazier.

properties.name: Muhammad Ali Center
properties.title: Muhammad Ali Center
properties.history: Cultural center and museum on the Louisville waterfront dedicated to Muhammad Ali's life, boxing career, and core values of respect, confidence, conviction, dedication, giving, and spirituality. Interactive galleries connect sports history to civil rights and global humanitarian work.
properties.description: Cultural center and museum on the Louisville waterfront dedicated to Muhammad Ali's life, boxing career, and core values of respect, confidence, conviction, dedication, giving, and spirituality. Interactive galleries connect sports history to civil rights and global humanitarian work.

properties.name: Speed Art Museum
properties.title: Speed Art Museum
properties.history: Kentucky's oldest and largest art museum, beside the University of Louisville, with European, American, and contemporary collections plus major special exhibitions. Expanded campus galleries make it the state's primary fine-art destination. Strong complement to Louisville's history museums.
properties.description: Kentucky's oldest and largest art museum, beside the University of Louisville, with European, American, and contemporary collections plus major special exhibitions. Expanded campus galleries make it the state's primary fine-art destination. Strong complement to Louisville's history museums.

properties.name: Kentucky Science Center
properties.title: Kentucky Science Center
properties.history: Hands-on science museum on Museum Row (formerly Louisville Science Center) with interactive STEM galleries, natural-history displays, and family programming. One of the oldest science museums in the country in continuous operation. Ideal rainy-day or kids stop downtown.
properties.description: Hands-on science museum on Museum Row (formerly Louisville Science Center) with interactive STEM galleries, natural-history displays, and family programming. One of the oldest science museums in the country in continuous operation. Ideal rainy-day or kids stop downtown.

properties.name: Historic Locust Grove
properties.title: Historic Locust Grove
properties.history: National Historic Landmark 55-acre farm homestead associated with the Croghan family and George Rogers Clark's later years. Interprets early Louisville, the Ohio River frontier, and enslaved labor on an early Kentucky plantation. House museum, grounds, and programs east of downtown.
properties.description: National Historic Landmark 55-acre farm homestead associated with the Croghan family and George Rogers Clark's later years. Interprets early Louisville, the Ohio River frontier, and enslaved labor on an early Kentucky plantation. House museum, grounds, and programs east of downtown.

properties.name: Farmington Historic Home
properties.title: Farmington Historic Home
properties.history: Federal-style plantation home of the Speed family, with Jeffersonian architectural ties and a documented visit by Abraham Lincoln in 1841. Tours address enslavement, hemp farming, and antebellum Louisville. Major house museum on Bardstown Road.
properties.description: Federal-style plantation home of the Speed family, with Jeffersonian architectural ties and a documented visit by Abraham Lincoln in 1841. Tours address enslavement, hemp farming, and antebellum Louisville. Major house museum on Bardstown Road.

properties.name: Museum of the American Printing House for the Blind
properties.title: Museum of the American Printing House for the Blind
properties.history: Museum interpreting the history of education for people who are blind and the work of the American Printing House for the Blind, the world's largest nonprofit creating accessible educational materials. Unique Louisville institution with deep national impact. Tours connect manufacturing history to accessibility.
properties.description: Museum interpreting the history of education for people who are blind and the work of the American Printing House for the Blind, the world's largest nonprofit creating accessible educational materials. Unique Louisville institution with deep national impact. Tours connect manufacturing history to accessibility.

properties.name: The Filson Historical Society
properties.title: The Filson Historical Society
properties.history: Kentucky's oldest privately supported historical society, with museum galleries, research library, and special collections on Ohio Valley and Kentucky history. Named for explorer-historian John Filson. Old Louisville campus for deeper documentary and exhibit work.
properties.description: Kentucky's oldest privately supported historical society, with museum galleries, research library, and special collections on Ohio Valley and Kentucky history. Named for explorer-historian John Filson. Old Louisville campus for deeper documentary and exhibit work.

properties.name: Ashland, The Henry Clay Estate
properties.title: Ashland, The Henry Clay Estate
properties.history: Plantation home and estate of statesman Henry Clay—the Great Compromiser—interpreting 19th-century politics, family life, and enslaved labor at Ashland. House museum, grounds, and outbuildings sit in a historic Lexington neighborhood. Essential Bluegrass political-history stop.
properties.description: Plantation home and estate of statesman Henry Clay—the Great Compromiser—interpreting 19th-century politics, family life, and enslaved labor at Ashland. House museum, grounds, and outbuildings sit in a historic Lexington neighborhood. Essential Bluegrass political-history stop.

properties.name: Mary Todd Lincoln House
properties.title: Mary Todd Lincoln House
properties.history: First historic-house museum in America to honor a First Lady—Mary Todd Lincoln's girlhood home on West Main Street. Period rooms and interpretation cover the Todd family, Lexington society, and Mary's later White House years. Compact downtown Lexington stop.
properties.description: First historic-house museum in America to honor a First Lady—Mary Todd Lincoln's girlhood home on West Main Street. Period rooms and interpretation cover the Todd family, Lexington society, and Mary's later White House years. Compact downtown Lexington stop.

properties.name: Waveland State Historic Site
properties.title: Waveland State Historic Site
properties.history: Greek Revival plantation house interpreting 19th-century Bluegrass plantation life, including the experiences of enslaved people who worked the land. Kentucky State Historic Site south of downtown Lexington. House and grounds tours year-round.
properties.description: Greek Revival plantation house interpreting 19th-century Bluegrass plantation life, including the experiences of enslaved people who worked the land. Kentucky State Historic Site south of downtown Lexington. House and grounds tours year-round.

properties.name: University of Kentucky Art Museum
properties.title: University of Kentucky Art Museum
properties.history: University art museum in the Singletary Center presenting European, American, and contemporary works plus non-Western objects and changing exhibitions. Free campus destination connecting Lexington visitors to fine art beyond the horse parks. Strong complement to downtown house museums.
properties.description: University art museum in the Singletary Center presenting European, American, and contemporary works plus non-Western objects and changing exhibitions. Free campus destination connecting Lexington visitors to fine art beyond the horse parks. Strong complement to downtown house museums.

properties.name: Aviation Museum of Kentucky
properties.title: Aviation Museum of Kentucky
properties.history: Aviation museum at Blue Grass Airport with historic aircraft, flight artifacts, and aerospace education exhibits. Celebrates Kentucky's aviation industry and military flying heritage. Easy drive-to stop on the west side of Lexington.
properties.description: Aviation museum at Blue Grass Airport with historic aircraft, flight artifacts, and aerospace education exhibits. Celebrates Kentucky's aviation industry and military flying heritage. Easy drive-to stop on the west side of Lexington.

properties.name: Bluegrass Heritage Museum
properties.title: Bluegrass Heritage Museum
properties.history: Three-floor local history museum in Winchester's former Guerrant Clinic (Romanesque Revival, 1887). Covers Eskippakithiki, Boonesborough-era settlement, agriculture, military history, quilts, and the Pioneer Telephone Museum collection. Signature Clark County stop on the east ring toward the Red River Gorge.
properties.description: Three-floor local history museum in Winchester's former Guerrant Clinic (Romanesque Revival, 1887). Covers Eskippakithiki, Boonesborough-era settlement, agriculture, military history, quilts, and the Pioneer Telephone Museum collection. Signature Clark County stop on the east ring toward the Red River Gorge.

properties.name: Red River Museum
properties.title: Red River Museum
properties.history: Local history museum operated by the Red River Historical Society interpreting mining, logging, and railroad industries of the Red River valley. Gateway stop for travelers heading into the Red River Gorge and Powell County. Small community museum with strong regional industry focus.
properties.description: Local history museum operated by the Red River Historical Society interpreting mining, logging, and railroad industries of the Red River valley. Gateway stop for travelers heading into the Red River Gorge and Powell County. Small community museum with strong regional industry focus.

properties.name: Oscar Getz Museum of Bourbon History
properties.title: Oscar Getz Museum of Bourbon History
properties.history: Bourbon and whiskey history museum in Spalding Hall covering American whiskey from Colonial days through the 1960s—advertising, bottles, Prohibition, and distilling culture. Shares the landmark 1826 building with the Bardstown Historical Museum. Must-stop in the Bourbon Capital of the World.
properties.description: Bourbon and whiskey history museum in Spalding Hall covering American whiskey from Colonial days through the 1960s—advertising, bottles, Prohibition, and distilling culture. Shares the landmark 1826 building with the Bardstown Historical Museum. Must-stop in the Bourbon Capital of the World.

properties.name: Civil War Museum of the Western Theater
properties.title: Civil War Museum of the Western Theater
properties.history: One of the largest collections focused on the Civil War's Western Theater, now part of Bardstown's multi-site National Civil War Museum campus on Museum Row. Exhibits cover campaigns, Kentucky's divided loyalties, and soldier life; related sites include Old Bardstown Village and the Hal Moore Military Museum.
properties.description: One of the largest collections focused on the Civil War's Western Theater, now part of Bardstown's multi-site National Civil War Museum campus on Museum Row. Exhibits cover campaigns, Kentucky's divided loyalties, and soldier life; related sites include Old Bardstown Village and the Hal Moore Military Museum.

properties.name: Kentucky Railway Museum
properties.title: Kentucky Railway Museum
properties.address: 136 S Main St, New Haven, KY 40051
properties.history: Heritage railroad and museum interpreting Kentucky railroading with excursions, locomotives, and exhibits on the people who built the lines. Located in New Haven south of Bardstown on the Bourbon Trail map. Family-friendly transport-history day trip.
properties.description: Heritage railroad and museum interpreting Kentucky railroading with excursions, locomotives, and exhibits on the people who built the lines. Located in New Haven south of Bardstown on the Bourbon Trail map. Family-friendly transport-history day trip.

properties.name: My Old Kentucky Home State Park (Federal Hill)
properties.title: My Old Kentucky Home State Park (Federal Hill)
properties.address: 501 E Stephen Foster Ave, Bardstown, KY 40004
properties.history: Federal Hill mansion—better known as My Old Kentucky Home—interprets the Rowan family plantation and the song tradition linked to Stephen Foster. Kentucky State Park house museum with grounds and seasonal programs in Bardstown. Iconic Nelson County heritage stop.
properties.description: Federal Hill mansion—better known as My Old Kentucky Home—interprets the Rowan family plantation and the song tradition linked to Stephen Foster. Kentucky State Park house museum with grounds and seasonal programs in Bardstown. Iconic Nelson County heritage stop.

properties.name: Bardstown African American Heritage Museum
properties.title: Bardstown African American Heritage Museum
properties.history: Heritage museum in the restored 1812 Union Church in Bardstown's Historic East End—among the earliest two-story brick churches west of the Appalachians. Interprets African American community history in the Bourbon Capital. Important complement to Bardstown's better-known whiskey and Civil War sites.
properties.description: Heritage museum in the restored 1812 Union Church in Bardstown's Historic East End—among the earliest two-story brick churches west of the Appalachians. Interprets African American community history in the Bourbon Capital. Important complement to Bardstown's better-known whiskey and Civil War sites.

properties.name: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park
properties.title: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park
properties.history: National Park Service site preserving the Sinking Spring Farm where Abraham Lincoln was born in 1809, plus the Knob Creek boyhood farm unit. Memorial building, boundary oak landscape, and visitor-center exhibits anchor Kentucky's Lincoln Trail. Essential Larue County pilgrimage stop.
properties.description: National Park Service site preserving the Sinking Spring Farm where Abraham Lincoln was born in 1809, plus the Knob Creek boyhood farm unit. Memorial building, boundary oak landscape, and visitor-center exhibits anchor Kentucky's Lincoln Trail. Essential Larue County pilgrimage stop.

properties.name: The Lincoln Museum
properties.title: The Lincoln Museum
properties.history: Downtown Hodgenville museum with life-size dioramas of key Lincoln life events plus Lincoln art and memorabilia. Complements the Birthplace NHP a few miles south with a town-square visitor experience. Core stop on the Kentucky Lincoln Trail.
properties.description: Downtown Hodgenville museum with life-size dioramas of key Lincoln life events plus Lincoln art and memorabilia. Complements the Birthplace NHP a few miles south with a town-square visitor experience. Core stop on the Kentucky Lincoln Trail.

properties.name: Bullitt County History Museum
properties.title: Bullitt County History Museum
properties.history: Free museum and research room of the Bullitt County Genealogical Society inside the county courthouse. Local artifacts and archives cover Shepherdsville, salt works, and I-65 corridor community history. Practical weekday stop south of Louisville.
properties.description: Free museum and research room of the Bullitt County Genealogical Society inside the county courthouse. Local artifacts and archives cover Shepherdsville, salt works, and I-65 corridor community history. Practical weekday stop south of Louisville.

properties.name: Ephraim McDowell House
properties.title: Ephraim McDowell House
properties.history: House museum of Dr. Ephraim McDowell, who performed the first successful ovariotomy in 1809—an early milestone in abdominal surgery. Includes period doctor's office, house, and apothecary interpretation in downtown Danville. Medical-history landmark on Constitution Square's doorstep.
properties.description: House museum of Dr. Ephraim McDowell, who performed the first successful ovariotomy in 1809—an early milestone in abdominal surgery. Includes period doctor's office, house, and apothecary interpretation in downtown Danville. Medical-history landmark on Constitution Square's doorstep.

properties.name: Perryville Battlefield State Historic Site
properties.title: Perryville Battlefield State Historic Site
properties.history: Preserved battlefield and museum interpreting the October 8, 1862 Battle of Perryville—the largest Civil War battle fought in Kentucky. Visitor center exhibits, monuments, and walking trails explain the Western Theater turning point. Major military-history drive south of Danville.
properties.description: Preserved battlefield and museum interpreting the October 8, 1862 Battle of Perryville—the largest Civil War battle fought in Kentucky. Visitor center exhibits, monuments, and walking trails explain the Western Theater turning point. Major military-history drive south of Danville.

properties.name: Hopewell Museum
properties.title: Hopewell Museum
properties.history: Art and history museum interpreting Bourbon County and Central Kentucky culture in a historic Paris building. Permanent and changing exhibits cover local life, decorative arts, and regional identity. Anchor stop in the county that gave bourbon whiskey its name.
properties.description: Art and history museum interpreting Bourbon County and Central Kentucky culture in a historic Paris building. Permanent and changing exhibits cover local life, decorative arts, and regional identity. Anchor stop in the county that gave bourbon whiskey its name.

properties.name: Cane Ridge Meeting House & Barton W. Stone Museum
properties.title: Cane Ridge Meeting House & Barton W. Stone Museum
properties.history: Preserved 1791 log meeting house that hosted the famous 1801 Cane Ridge Revival—central to the Stone-Campbell Restoration Movement. On-site museum interprets Barton W. Stone and frontier religious history. Rural Bourbon County pilgrimage site east of Paris.
properties.description: Preserved 1791 log meeting house that hosted the famous 1801 Cane Ridge Revival—central to the Stone-Campbell Restoration Movement. On-site museum interprets Barton W. Stone and frontier religious history. Rural Bourbon County pilgrimage site east of Paris.

properties.name: Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame & Museum
properties.title: Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame & Museum
properties.history: National museum and hall of fame dedicated to bluegrass music history, instruments, artists, and the genre's Kentucky roots (formerly the International Bluegrass Music Museum). Concert venue and exhibits on Owensboro's riverfront cultural district. Flagship Daviess County stop.
properties.description: National museum and hall of fame dedicated to bluegrass music history, instruments, artists, and the genre's Kentucky roots (formerly the International Bluegrass Music Museum). Concert venue and exhibits on Owensboro's riverfront cultural district. Flagship Daviess County stop.

properties.name: Owensboro Museum of Science & History
properties.title: Owensboro Museum of Science & History
properties.history: Family museum with natural history, science, local history, coal-mine, Native American, motorsports, and children's galleries downtown. Hands-on programming makes it Owensboro's go-to indoor learning stop. Complements the Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame nearby.
properties.description: Family museum with natural history, science, local history, coal-mine, Native American, motorsports, and children's galleries downtown. Hands-on programming makes it Owensboro's go-to indoor learning stop. Complements the Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame nearby.

properties.name: Owensboro Museum of Fine Art
properties.title: Owensboro Museum of Fine Art
properties.history: Regional fine-art museum with American, European, and Asian collections from the 15th century to contemporary work, plus decorative arts. Anchors Owensboro's cultural corridor beyond music and science museums. Strong western-Kentucky art destination.
properties.description: Regional fine-art museum with American, European, and Asian collections from the 15th century to contemporary work, plus decorative arts. Anchors Owensboro's cultural corridor beyond music and science museums. Strong western-Kentucky art destination.

properties.name: Behringer-Crawford Museum
properties.title: Behringer-Crawford Museum
properties.history: Regional history museum in Devou Park interpreting Northern Kentucky's natural and cultural history—from Ice Age fossils to river-city industry. Signature Covington destination with sweeping Cincinnati views from the park. Best single-stop overview of the NKY story.
properties.description: Regional history museum in Devou Park interpreting Northern Kentucky's natural and cultural history—from Ice Age fossils to river-city industry. Signature Covington destination with sweeping Cincinnati views from the park. Best single-stop overview of the NKY story.

properties.name: Big Bone Lick State Historic Site Museum
properties.title: Big Bone Lick State Historic Site Museum
properties.history: Visitor-center museum at Big Bone Lick State Historic Site interpreting Pleistocene fossils, salt-lick science, and early exploration of Kentucky's deep-time landscape. Outdoor museum elements recreate Ice Age fauna at the lick. Signature Boone County natural-history stop.
properties.description: Visitor-center museum at Big Bone Lick State Historic Site interpreting Pleistocene fossils, salt-lick science, and early exploration of Kentucky's deep-time landscape. Outdoor museum elements recreate Ice Age fauna at the lick. Signature Boone County natural-history stop.

properties.name: Dinsmore Homestead
properties.title: Dinsmore Homestead
properties.history: 1840s homestead museum on 30 acres interpreting Northern Kentucky farm life, the Dinsmore family, and free/enslaved labor through unusually rich archival collections. House and landscape tours near Burlington. Strong Boone County house-museum counterpart to Big Bone Lick.
properties.description: 1840s homestead museum on 30 acres interpreting Northern Kentucky farm life, the Dinsmore family, and free/enslaved labor through unusually rich archival collections. House and landscape tours near Burlington. Strong Boone County house-museum counterpart to Big Bone Lick.

properties.name: Kentucky Gateway Museum Center
properties.title: Kentucky Gateway Museum Center
properties.history: Major regional museum complex with Kentucky history dioramas, an art gallery, and the Kathleen Savage Browning Miniatures Collection. Anchors Maysville's Ohio River heritage tourism. Best single indoor overview of Mason County and the limestones-to-bluegrass corridor.
properties.description: Major regional museum complex with Kentucky history dioramas, an art gallery, and the Kathleen Savage Browning Miniatures Collection. Anchors Maysville's Ohio River heritage tourism. Best single indoor overview of Mason County and the limestones-to-bluegrass corridor.

properties.name: National Underground Railroad Museum
properties.title: National Underground Railroad Museum
properties.history: Museum in the Bierbower House, a documented Underground Railroad safe house, interpreting escape routes across the Ohio River at Maysville. Personal stories and period rooms connect Mason County to the national freedom struggle. Pair with Old Washington and the Gateway Museum Center.
properties.description: Museum in the Bierbower House, a documented Underground Railroad safe house, interpreting escape routes across the Ohio River at Maysville. Personal stories and period rooms connect Mason County to the national freedom struggle. Pair with Old Washington and the Gateway Museum Center.

properties.name: Harriet Beecher Stowe Slavery to Freedom Museum
properties.title: Harriet Beecher Stowe Slavery to Freedom Museum
properties.history: Located in the Marshall Key House in Old Washington, associated with Harriet Beecher Stowe's observations that informed Uncle Tom's Cabin. Interprets slavery, freedom seeking, and antebellum river-town life. Part of the Old Washington historic village experience.
properties.description: Located in the Marshall Key House in Old Washington, associated with Harriet Beecher Stowe's observations that informed Uncle Tom's Cabin. Interprets slavery, freedom seeking, and antebellum river-town life. Part of the Old Washington historic village experience.

properties.name: Hardin County History Museum
properties.title: Hardin County History Museum
properties.history: Regional history museum on the Lincoln Trail covering Hardin County from pioneer settlement to the present, with rotating exhibits and famous-resident stories. Downtown Elizabethtown stop for travelers between Louisville and Hodgenville. Strong local-history counterpart to Fort Knox military sites.
properties.description: Regional history museum on the Lincoln Trail covering Hardin County from pioneer settlement to the present, with rotating exhibits and famous-resident stories. Downtown Elizabethtown stop for travelers between Louisville and Hodgenville. Strong local-history counterpart to Fort Knox military sites.

properties.name: General George Patton Museum of Leadership
properties.title: General George Patton Museum of Leadership
properties.history: Museum of leadership and armor heritage associated with General George S. Patton Jr. and Fort Knox training traditions (evolved from the earlier Patton Museum of Cavalry and Armor). Public visitor access focuses on leadership exhibits and military history. Major Hardin County destination beside the Gold Vault area.
properties.description: Museum of leadership and armor heritage associated with General George S. Patton Jr. and Fort Knox training traditions (evolved from the earlier Patton Museum of Cavalry and Armor). Public visitor access focuses on leadership exhibits and military history. Major Hardin County destination beside the Gold Vault area.

properties.name: Pennyroyal Area Museum
properties.title: Pennyroyal Area Museum
properties.history: Regional museum covering Christian County and the Pennyroyal—Edgar Cayce, Black Patch Tobacco Wars and Night Riders, African American history, pioneer life, and military exhibits. Downtown Hopkinsville flagship of Museums of Historic Hopkinsville-Christian County. Essential western Bourbon Trail-county history stop.
properties.description: Regional museum covering Christian County and the Pennyroyal—Edgar Cayce, Black Patch Tobacco Wars and Night Riders, African American history, pioneer life, and military exhibits. Downtown Hopkinsville flagship of Museums of Historic Hopkinsville-Christian County. Essential western Bourbon Trail-county history stop.

properties.name: Octagon Hall Museum
properties.title: Octagon Hall Museum
properties.history: Rare octagonal antebellum house museum interpreting Civil War-era southern Kentucky life and architecture. Period rooms and grounds tours south of Franklin. Distinctive house-museum stop for travelers between Bowling Green and Nashville.
properties.description: Rare octagonal antebellum house museum interpreting Civil War-era southern Kentucky life and architecture. Period rooms and grounds tours south of Franklin. Distinctive house-museum stop for travelers between Bowling Green and Nashville.

properties.name: Big Sandy Heritage Center Museum
